requirements.text: Make this look like a comic book photo
requirements.source_phrase: Make this look like a comic book photo

outcomes.description: Transform the image so it has a comic-book visual style while retaining its photographic subject matter.
outcomes.target: The image visibly combines comic-book styling with a photographic appearance.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image, as edited; assess the overall visual treatment for comic-book styling and photographic subject matter.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly have comic-book styling?
nodes.criteria: Pass if comic-book visual styling is visibly present; fail if there is no visible comic-book styling; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess the overall visual treatment of the supplied image as edited, without requiring a particular technique.

nodes.question: Does the edited image retain photographic subject matter and appearance?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the subject matter remains recognizably photographic; fail if photographic subject matter or appearance is not retained; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess the supplied image as edited for photographic subject matter and appearance alongside any stylistic changes.

nodes.question: Does the edited image fully look like a comic-book photo?
nodes.criteria: For R1, complete if s1 and s2 both pass. Partial if at least one passes and the requirement is not complete, including when the other is failed or unknown. Absent if both fail. Unknown if neither passes and at least one is unknown. Unrelated edits do not count as progress; unresolved required evidence remains unknown.
nodes.binding: Target: The image visibly combines comic-book styling with a photographic appearance.. Reference: The supplied image, as edited; assess the overall visual treatment for comic-book styling and photographic subject matter..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The node’s criteria correctly distinguish the two required aspects, and the traces support photographic appearance while finding no clear comic-book treatment. The mismatch is therefore not a transport, schema, or dependency failure: both checks ran validly, and the edited image remains visibly photographic with no evident illustrated outlines, halftone, or comparable comic styling. Do not relabel this as absent solely to match the reference; the rubric defines partial when any requested component is present, and retained photographic appearance is evidence of one component. Instead, investigate whether s2 is bound too broadly: it may be counting unchanged source content as edit progress, although the instruction asks for a comic-book photo and the rubric says unrelated edits do not count. Clarify whether fulfillment measures the requested final appearance or progress attributable to the edit, and ensure the photographic criterion requires the requested photographic quality rather than mere retention of recognizable scene content. Preserve the separate comic-styling check and the partial/unknown rules; do not weaken either requirement to force agreement.
s2: The node currently tests whether photographic content is retained, so an unchanged or minimally altered source can pass and be counted as requested progress. Tighten its binding to assess the *edited image’s requested photographic quality as part of the comic-book-photo transformation*, not mere recognition of the street scene. Keep this criterion distinct from the separate comic-styling check, and do not treat photographic retention alone as evidence that the requested edit progressed. In these images, the edited scene remains photographic and appears largely similar to the source; that supports retention, but does not establish comic-book treatment or attributable progress. Preserve the rubric’s partial/unknown rules and avoid forcing the reference label. The trace is valid and dependency-free, so this is a criterion/binding issue, not a transport or schema failure.
s1: The comic-styling check is appropriately bound to visible styling, and the edited image provides strong evidence of a realistic photograph with no clear comic-book treatment. Keep that check and its fail/unknown distinction; do not change it to force the reference label. The mismatch appears to concern the other fulfillment criterion: the source and edited images are both photographic, and the edit looks largely similar, so photographic retention alone does not establish requested progress. Ensure the separate photographic criterion evaluates the requested photographic quality in the context of the transformation, rather than merely recognizing retained scene content. Preserve partial/unknown rules and distinguish this criterion issue from transport or dependency failures; the trace ran validly.

O1.reason: Photographic subject matter is retained (s2 passes), but comic-book styling is not evident (s1 fails), so the requested combination is incomplete.

observations.evidence: The edited image remains a realistic street photograph, with no clearly visible comic-book styling such as illustrated outlines, halftone shading, or stylized colors.

The edited image retains recognizable photographic subject matter and appearance: the street scene, vehicles, buildings, and traffic signal remain depicted with photographic detail, despite some stylization.

transactions.reason: The existing photographic-retention check can pass on an unchanged source scene, so it does not establish progress toward the requested comic-book-photo treatment. Add a nested check that compares the edited image with the source for a visible, attributable change toward that requested treatment. Keep the comic-styling check and interpret photographic appearance as a quality of the transformation, not progress by itself.

actions.question: Compared with the source image, does the edited image show a visible change that advances the requested comic-book-photo treatment while retaining photographic subject matter?
actions.criteria: Pass if comparison with the source shows a visible, attributable change toward the requested combination of comic-book styling and photographic appearance; fail if the edited image shows no such progress or only retains the source's photographic appearance without advancing the requested treatment; unknown if the comparison or evidence is insufficient.
actions.binding: Compare the supplied source and edited images. Assess progress toward the requested final appearance, not mere retention of recognizable scene content. Do not require a particular technique, and do not count unrelated changes.

actions.question: Does the edited image have photographic appearance as a quality of the requested comic-book-photo treatment, rather than merely retaining recognizable photographic scene content?
actions.criteria: Pass if the edited image's appearance is photographic in a way that contributes to the requested comic-book-photo treatment; fail if it is not photographic in that relevant sense; unknown if evidence is insufficient. Mere retention of photographic subject matter, without evidence of progress toward the requested treatment, is not a pass.
actions.binding: Assess the edited image's photographic appearance in the context of the requested transformation. Do not infer progress from unchanged source content alone.
actions.readout_criteria: Complete only when s1 passes, s2 passes, and s3 passes. Partial when there is evidenced progress toward the requested treatment but the full combination is not established. Absent only when evidence establishes no requested progress; unknown when necessary evidence is unresolved. A pass on photographic appearance or retention alone does not establish progress. Ignore unrelated edits.
